title: [Core] Try to explicitly get StringName in `_call_bind`

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Original PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118507

`_call_bind` multi-threaded debug improvements depends on https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118803.
Improves multi-threaded speed of `_call_bind` in release build.

## Technical overview
Explicitly tries to get reference to the string name if the Variant is string name.

I tried to use ternary 
```cpp
const StringName &method = (p_args[0]->get_type() == Variant::STRING_NAME) ? *VariantInternal::get_string_name(p_args[0])  : static_cast<StringName>(*VariantInternal::get_string(p_args[0]));
```
to have less changes, but it didn't improve anything, so the current PR handles them separately.

Only improves speed if the variant is `StringName`, if it is `String` the speed will be the same as in the current master. Tbh not sure if it is possible to pass `String` here, but it will handle it correctly.

## Performace testing
Build commands are the same as in the original PR.
Test project: [testthreads4.6_target.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26926113/testthreads4.6_target.zip)

The basic test was to divide the iterations between threads and to perform the most basic interaction inside the loop, in theory this should imitate doing parallelizable work. The number of iterations was 200_000_000.

The results are presented as tables. In the columns was written the number of threads this attempt used, 0th thread is main thread that serves as the control.
Column type:
- `debug` - tested it in launched from Godot project
- `tool` - tested it inside tool script in editor
- `release` - tested it in export release

Tested on:
- EndeavourOS on X11 
- X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors 
- Vulkan (Forward+) 
- dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (nvidia; 595.58.03) 
- Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-9300H CPU @ 2.40GHz (8 threads) 
- 15.49 GiB memory

Includes additional case with lock-free `ObjectDB::get_instance` on top of current changes. 

<details>
<summary>func_base, this one is fine, control</summary>
Setting values directly on the instance fields is also fine

```gdscript
func func_base(count: int) -> int:
    var time_before: int = Time.get_ticks_msec()
    var sum := 0
    for i in count:
        sum += 1
    finished.emit.call_deferred(Time.get_ticks_msec() - time_before)
    return sum
```

<details>
<summary>call_bind, kind of strange</summary>

```gdscript
func call_bind(count: int) -> int:
    var time_before: int = Time.get_ticks_msec()
    var sum := 0
    for i in count:
        sum += call(&"get_instance_increment")
    finished.emit.call_deferred(Time.get_ticks_msec() - time_before)
    return sum

func get_instance_increment() -> int:
    return 1
```
